step-limit.text: Run pauses Turing’s first machine after 10,000 steps. What does the pause tell you?

never-stops.why: The simulator cannot know that. It only counts steps.

not-yet.text: Only that the machine has not stopped yet
not-yet.why: Another machine might stop at step 10,001. The limit is a guess.

error.text: That the machine has an error
error.why: The machine works as its rules say. It just keeps going.

decider.text: What would the machine H in this lesson have to do?

run-and-wait.text: Run the other machine and wait for it to stop
run-and-wait.why: If the other machine runs forever, H would never answer.

some-machines.why: H must be right for every machine and every input.

always-answer.text: Always stop, and say correctly if any machine stops on any input
always-answer.why: That is the task, and the diagonal argument shows that no machine can do it.

print-zero.text: Print 0 when the other machine stops
print-zero.why: Printing 0 answers nothing. H must say “stops” or “forever”.

diagonal.text: D does the opposite of what H says about each machine on its own description. What happens when D gets its own description?

contradiction.text: Each possible answer of H turns out wrong
contradiction.why: If H says “stops”, D runs forever. If H says “forever”, D stops. So H cannot exist.

stops.text: D stops, and H is right
stops.why: If D stops, H said “forever”, so H is wrong.

forever.text: D runs forever, and H is right
forever.why: If D runs forever, H said “stops”, so H is wrong.

turing-proved.text: What did Turing prove in section 8 of his 1936 paper?

stops.text: That no machine can decide if a machine stops
stops.why: That is the form later authors used. Turing asked other questions.

every-machine-stops.text: That every machine stops in the end

circle-free-and-zero.text: That no machine can decide if a machine is circle-free, or if it ever prints 0
circle-free-and-zero.why: These are his two results, on pages 247 and 248.

circular.text: A machine prints 0, then 1, and then stops. What did Turing call it?

circular.why: It prints only a finite number of digits, so it is circular, a bad machine for Turing.

circle-free.why: A circle-free machine prints digits without end.

universal.why: The universal machine 𝒰 is the machine of lesson 3, which can do the work of any machine.
